articles.title: Workspaces and the guided builder
articles.body:
A workspace remembers folders, filenames, metadata, and review preferences for a kind of photography. Import and Organize have separate settings.

Choose a workspace

Use the window toolbar or Workspace menu. Open at Launch is separate from the active workspace. Control-0 selects Basic; Control-1 through Control-9 select assigned workspaces.

Create a workspace

Choose New Workspace…, then Use Workspace Builder for guided steps or Set Up Manually for direct access to the same sections. Changes stay in a draft until you choose Save Workspace. Cancel leaves your saved setup unchanged.

Preview a starting point

Start with Build from scratch, Events, Headshots, or Real Estate. Expand a starter to see its folders, filenames, and import questions. Expanding it only previews the setup; choose its Use button to apply it to your draft.

  • Build from scratch: a dated import folder and original camera filenames.
  • Events: a project with photo numbering that continues across cards, stacked bursts, and separate video folders.
  • Headshots: a project per client, session folders, similar-frame stacks, and a Selects destination for tagged photos.
  • Real Estate: address-based folders for originals, video, edits, exports, and floor plans, with exposure brackets stacked.

Applying another starter replaces the draft’s workflow choices. If you have edited the draft, review the confirmation before continuing. You can customize the result afterward.

Work through eight sections

Workspace, Import Folders, Import File Names, Organize, Browse & Review, Metadata, After Import, and Review & Save. Questions are part of the variables you insert; Photo Groups are configured in Import Settings.

Choose folders and filenames

Import Folders asks where photos go, whether each import gets its own folder, which empty folders to create for later work, which files you normally import, and whether to make a backup. Photos go here identifies the receiving folder. Empty Edits or Final Exports folders do not receive copies automatically.

Keep original filenames or build names from text and variables. Insert Variable offers Photo Number first, followed by other naming pieces and questions. Open What do the variables mean? for examples. Import and Organize retain independent destinations and naming patterns.

Ask only for details you use

Choose an answer variable such as Client or Shoot name, or add New Question… from Insert Variable. Questions are asked at import only when a folder name, filename, or metadata template uses them. Check You’ll be asked at import to see the actual questions. Project answers are reused for the job; shoot answers belong to that session.

Photo Groups are separate from folder grouping. Use them in Import Settings when a shoot needs named groups. Continuing the same shoot can retain group numbering across cards; a new shoot starts fresh. Review import scope and numbering before the next card.

Review and save

Review & Save summarizes Import and Organize separately, with Edit links to their sections. Check the examples, then choose Save Workspace. Use Workspace applies the saved setup; it does not start an import. Connect external destinations while configuring them and reselect a destination after renaming its drive.

Camera matching and Apple Photos

Camera matching can choose a workspace when a card opens; a workspace chosen by hand takes precedence. Apple Photos requires both Settings → General integration and the workspace’s Apple Photos switch. Focus Mode (F) hides surrounding controls without changing saved panel preferences.

articles.title: The Command Palette
articles.body:
If you can do it in Ingest, you can find it with ⌘K. Search for an action by name: review photos, edit metadata, change a view, organize files, or export. Use the arrow keys to select a result and Return to run it. Commands that cannot run in the current context explain why.

Commands with assigned shortcuts show them beside their names, so the Command Palette helps you learn the keys you use most. Commands that cannot run right now stay visible with the reason underneath, rather than vanishing and leaving you wondering. ⇧⌘P pins a command to the top for good.

Command descriptions explain what each action does. Settings → Command Palette controls descriptions, shortcut labels, and excluded commands. If you have hidden an action, you can restore it there.

The footer names the command Return will run. Click Actions or press ⌘K again to pin or unpin the highlighted command, copy its link, or configure its shortcut. Configure Shortcut opens that exact command in Settings. Copy Link keeps the palette open and confirms the copy. Esc closes Actions first, then the palette and returns focus to where you were.

Choose Find Folder… in the palette, or press ⇧⌘F, to search folders on your Mac and connected drives. ⌘F filters photos in the current collection. Show Left Sidebar, Show Right Sidebar, and Show Both Sidebars change the view for the current workspace.

Your favorites, workspaces, splits, presets, actions, and recent folders are all in there too, so the palette is a way to go somewhere as well as a way to do something. ? shows the shortcut sheet, and tapping and releasing ⌘, then pressing it again and holding, shows contextual shortcuts. A single Command hold does not open the overlay.

articles.title: Settings
articles.body:
⌘, opens a window with a search field. Everything the app stores is in there with a real control: folder and app choosers instead of typed paths, pickers instead of remembered strings, live previews for templates, snippets, and splits, and drag to reorder wherever the order decides a number key.

Ordinary app settings apply as you edit them. Workspace, template, and action editors use explicit Save and Cancel. Settings search filters the available results; choose a result or press Return to navigate to its control. Supported changes can be undone with ⌘Z while the window is open. Settings → Advanced exports configuration to carry to another Mac, described on the automation page.

There is one row that is not a setting. On the Browsing page, Memory cards are never modified has a lock beside it instead of a switch. It is listed so that the rule is visible, not so that it can be turned off.

Keywords

Keywords are descriptive words or phrases, separate from the on/off review tag. Ingest builds keyword suggestions from photographs it has read. Folders record their keywords as they are read, and the Photos library is read in full after it connects, so a keyword that exists only in Photos can appear in a folder’s keyword suggestions without opening Apple Photos. Photos keywords need macOS 27.

Settings → Keywords lists known keywords with their Photos counts and folder locations. Select one or more and rename, merge, change case, unify spellings, remove from suggestions, or delete.

Every change shows a preview first: how many photographs in Photos, how many files in each open folder, and how many files sit in folders that are not open, which keep the old spelling until you open them. Photos is changed in batches and a failed batch is reported without stopping the rest; open folders go through the verified metadata path and sit in Undo, and the receipt offers Revert.

articles.title: Cards and folders
articles.body:
Put a card in and it appears in the sources list. A newly inserted camera card opens in Browse when Settings → Transfers → Open a card when it is inserted is on. Cards connected before launch remain available in the sidebar. Press ⌘O to open a folder instead. Available previews load progressively while Ingest reads the source.

Click the sidebar magnifier, press ⇧⌘F, or choose Find Folder in ⌘K to search folder names in a roomy palette. Results include parent paths; Escape closes the palette without changing the tree. Current, recent, and favorite folders appear immediately, with other results supplied by Spotlight.

The sidebar keeps your Mac’s folder tree in place. Single-click a folder to navigate in the current Browse tab; double-click to open it in a new tab. Command-W closes the current tab before the window.

Favorites, Recent, and Saved Views have collapsible sections. Use Add to Favorites from the menu or command palette. ⌘D deselects photos. Show photos in subfolders is visible beside the folder name and defaults off; when enabled, selecting a photo identifies its containing folder. Finder’s Open With Ingest opens the photo’s folder and selects it.

⌘[ and ⌘] go back and forward through what you have opened, like a browser, so switching to the card and back to yesterday's folder costs one keystroke.

⌘E ejects. Ingest closes every file it has open on the card first, which is why eject does not fail with the usual complaint about a file in use. If a card disappears, Ingest closes the source and cancels an active import. Verified copies are retained; check the result for incomplete groups.

There is also a menu bar item, on by default, showing the progress of a running ingest, the cards that are in, and your recent folders. It is there so a copy can run while you work in another app.

After reconnecting a drive

Reopen the original source to recover its tags, ratings, and saved Organize draft. Check any interrupted import separately. Resume work after reconnecting →

articles.title: Browse, sort, and include subfolders
articles.body:
Choose Grid, Preview, Split, or List from the photo-view menu. ⌘1, ⌘2, and ⌘3 select Grid, Preview, and Split. Press I to cycle photo information. The inspector provides Histogram, Camera Details, Caption, Keywords, and Location; choose and reorder its sections in Settings → Sidebar Information.

Fast RAW previews

Ingest reads the camera’s embedded JPEG for fast RAW browsing. Preview size and resolution depend on the camera and recording mode.

No import is needed to browse. If no usable preview exists, Ingest renders the selected photo and caches it; the first render takes longer.

Move and select

Arrow keys move, ⇧ extends the selection, and ⌘ with an arrow moves the focus ring without disturbing what is selected. ⌘+ and ⌘- resize the thumbnails, and so does a pinch.

Sorting and filtering

Sort controls photo order. Browse by chooses an ordered hierarchy such as Day → Camera → Lens, which places photos under headings without filtering them. Selected dimensions stay together at the top of the checklist; drag or use the reorder controls to change their order. Stacks collect related burst, bracket, similar, or paired photographs.

While browsing under headings, click the group bar or a heading to jump to another group; [ and ] move between groups. These viewing choices are separate from the named Photo Groups used during import.

Sidebars and Focus Mode

Left and right sidebar buttons have matching View-menu and command-palette actions. Each workspace remembers visibility and resized widths. Tab and Shift-Tab move keyboard focus through controls. Focus Mode hides surrounding controls temporarily, while command-palette access remains available.

Include subfolders

Show photos in subfolders stays beside the source name, shortened to Subfolders in a compact window. The View menu and command palette share the same setting; search for “subfolders” or “recursive.” Ordinary folders start with it off. Camera subfolders are always included, and Apple Photos omits this filesystem control. Single-click a sidebar folder to navigate; Command-click opens it in another tab.

Photo background

Photo Background in Settings → General offers Appearance Default, Black, Dark Gray, Medium Gray, Light Gray, and White. A workspace can use the app default or its own override. Thumbnail Size shows a readout in Grid; Preview has Zoom controls.

Browse, Apple Photos, and Organize share photo controls appropriate to each context. Sort shows the current criterion and has a separate direction button. File views include capture time, filename, rating, color label, date modified, and file size; Apple Photos adds album order and Organize adds group order. Import Settings has its own photo scope and output preview.

Filter the view

Show chooses All, Tagged, Untagged, or Selected photos. Filters opens the editor for ratings, color labels, file kinds, and metadata. An active-filter summary explains what is limiting the view, and Clear All removes the filters. Choosing All in Show does not clear other filters. Saved views live in the filter editor, and ⇧⌘S saves the current filter as a new one.

Photographs are ordered by when they were taken, down to the fraction of a second, so two cameras at the same event interleave correctly. A folder remembers the order you left it in.

Which files are supported, and what happens to the rest, is on the support page.

articles.title: Apple Photos, inside Ingest
articles.body:
Connect your library

Choose Apple Photos in Sources and allow Photos access. Ingest uses your System Photo Library, not an arbitrary library file.

Integration is optional. Enable it in both Settings → General and the current workspace. Turning it off hides Photos controls but retains your saved review state and recipes. Finish active Photos operations first.

Find and browse photos

  • Choose Library, Favorites, or an album. Find albums filters the sidebar.
  • Unfiled shows photos outside ordinary albums; Unreviewed tracks your Ingest review progress.
  • Search by filename. Caption and keyword search requires macOS 27; the first library search may take time.
  • Choose Grid, Preview, or Split with ⌘1, ⌘2, or ⌘3. Space toggles Preview. Command-click or Shift-click selects several photos.

Work offline

Local photos work offline. Originals stored only in iCloud must download through Photos; a thumbnail may appear first. For offline access, choose Download Originals to this Mac in Photos → Settings → iCloud and let syncing finish. This uses more storage.

Review and file a selection

  • G: add selected photos to albums.
  • R: mark reviewed; ⇧R: mark and advance.
  • F: toggle a native Photos favorite in this context.
  • ⌥⌘S and ⌘I: toggle Sources and Inspector.

Tags, color labels, and reviewed marks stay in Ingest. Analysis starts when you choose Analyze Review Photos. The inspector loads detail as needed; its histogram describes the rendered Photos image.

Manage albums

Use the plus menu to create albums or folders, and context menus to rename or move them. In editable albums, ⌥⌘← and ⌥⌘→ reorder selected photos.

Delete removes photos from the current album. Delete from Library… is a separate confirmed action affecting every album, Recently Deleted, and iCloud Photos.

Edit metadata and organize

Press M to review metadata edits. Captions, keywords, and native star ratings require macOS 27. Favorites, capture dates, and locations work on earlier supported versions. Earlier-version ratings stay local; transferring them into Photos later requires review.

Organize Photos into Albums previews grouping, destination paths, assignments, and order. Apply adds to those albums without removing unrelated contents. Recipes run on demand; Shared Album publishing and native Smart Album rule editing are not included.

Send files to Apple Photos

  1. Select photos in a writable folder and choose Send to Apple Photos….
  2. Review the destination album and format. The default uses JPEGs or JPEG companions and skips files without one. Choose RAW explicitly if wanted; RAW + JPEG creates separate Photos assets.
  3. Confirm the reviewed import. Ingest stages verified copies and leaves source files unchanged.

Memory cards must finish import and backups first. Organize offers Send Groups to Photos…; after-import actions use the same reviewed flow.

Check imports and duplicates

Receipts recognize previous Ingest imports by content hash; they do not scan your whole Photos library for duplicates. Use Photos Import History to reconcile uncertain results. Allow a New Import deliberately retries and may create a duplicate. A successful import does not confirm iCloud upload.

Send to Decks

Select stills and choose Send to Decks… (⇧⌘E). Ingest prepares the rendered images, downloading if needed, for a new or existing Decks project.

Photos changes can sync when iCloud Photos is enabled. Photos privacy and storage →

articles.title: Video
articles.body:
Clips sit in the grid alongside the photographs with a poster frame and their length. Space plays. J, K, and L shuttle the way they do in every editor, , and . step a frame, and M mutes.

↑ and ↓ always move to the next item rather than doing something to the video, so a clip never traps you in the middle of a cull.

Sony clips carry a small sidecar file with the real creation time. Ingest reads it, so clips sort into the right place among the photographs, and it copies the sidecar alongside the clip when you ingest.

articles.title: Review photos and choose keepers
articles.body:
Review a set of photos

Choose Review in Browse’s photo-control row, the photo context menu, or the command palette. Multiple selected photos form a fixed queue; otherwise Review uses the visible photos starting at the active photo. Videos are excluded, and marking does not remove photos from the queue.

Inspect faces and focus

The review queue keeps the set available while you inspect a photo. The inspection area shows Faces close-ups and focus detail. Click a face or use [ and ] to zoom to it; Fit returns to the whole photo. Corrections belong to individual faces or detail. Uncertain eyes are explained in the selected face’s details, rather than repeated under every thumbnail. Sharper eye reassessment runs for the inspected photo, not the whole folder.

Compare candidates

Compare… holds a reference while the filmstrip chooses candidates; inspection and marks follow the active pane. Back to Review restores the prior photo, face, zoom, and inspection scroll. Done restores Browse or Suggestions with its selection, filters, and scroll position; your saved decisions remain.

Optional assistance

Optional Second Opinion: find Ask Claude for a Second Opinion… in ⌘K for selected photos, or ask about the current folder or album. Review the scope, type a question, and choose Ask. It requires Claude Code and your Claude account, and sends requested previews and details to Anthropic. It can navigate your viewer but cannot change marks or files. What is shared →

Review entirely by hand or use optional built-in on-device assistance for eye and sharpness assessments, similar-photo evaluation, and keeper suggestions. You review and apply suggestions; opening them does not change your tags. Photo analysis stays on your Mac.

Tag, rate, and mark reviewed

T toggles a tag and U removes it. Tag photos to find or act on them together. Stars, colors, and keywords are independent: 1 to 5 set stars, and pressing the current rating clears it. 6 to 9 set color labels, with ⌥9 for purple. R marks it reviewed.

By default a marking key changes the current photo without advancing. Turn on advancing in Settings → Browsing and the loop becomes one key per photograph: T to keep, → to skip. Holding ⇧ with any marking key does the opposite for that one press.

Use ⌘Z to undo review marks, batches of marks, and supported stack changes.

Where marks are saved

Tags live in Ingest. For writable folders, stars and color labels are saved in supported image files or XMP sidecars, so compatible editing apps can read them. Writes run in the background. On a memory card, Ingest keeps review changes locally and applies them to the copies during import.

Delete photos

Press Delete or right-click a photo to delete it. Confirmation is enabled by default; change it in Settings or in the confirmation dialog. All shows every photo in the current folder scope, and Untagged shows every photo without a tag.

articles.title: Review decisions and protection
articles.body:
T tags the selected photos, or clears their tags when all are already tagged. R marks reviewed. Stars and labels stay independent. Use the visible Show: All / Tagged / Untagged / Selected controls to narrow the grid. More Filters adds capture dates, kind, and analysis. Before and After exclude the chosen day; Between includes both complete days.

Protect / Unlock Photos controls editing inside Ingest. Protected photos remain viewable and copyable, and disabled editing controls explain “Protected. Unlock to edit.” Mixed selections report protected exclusions. Keyword drafts stay open if a write fails.

Import… opens Import Settings. Its initial scope is Selected when photos are selected, otherwise All; choose Tagged explicitly for keepers. Display filters do not change import membership, and empty scopes stay empty. The eligible set freezes when copying starts. Protected originals remain protected; delete-copied cleanup requires verified, unprotected files. Import scope and verification →

articles.title: The preview
articles.body:
Space opens the large view, and Space again closes it. ⌘1, ⌘2, and ⌘3 switch between grid, preview, and both at once.

In the grid, hold Z over a thumbnail to show the loupe, then release to dismiss it. Hovering does not change selection. Loading or limited-resolution labels tell you when full detail is not available. The View menu can keep Grid Loupe enabled; Settings holds its size and magnification.

In Preview, Z goes to 100% at the pointer, so whatever is under the cursor stays under the cursor, and Z again returns to fit. ⌥1, ⌥2, and ⌥4 are fixed zoom levels, and ⇧F fits. F toggles Focus mode. A pinch, a two finger drag, and a two finger double tap do the same things.

The zoom is sticky as you move between photographs, which is the point: you set 100% on an eye, then arrow through five frames and compare the same eye in each.

In ordinary preview mode, at 100% Ingest shows the full size JPEG from inside the raw file, whose size depends on the camera and recording mode. When a raw file's preview is smaller than its JPEG twin, Ingest uses the twin, and the information overlay tells you which pixels you are actually judging.

See saved Adobe edits

For a RAW photo, choose Preview with Adobe Edits in the Command Palette. Requires Adobe DNG Converter and edits saved to the file or sidecar. Set up and refresh an Adobe preview →

articles.title: Compare and survey
articles.body:
C opens Select on the left and Candidate on the right. Candidates come from an explicit multiselection, then the current stack, then the filtered source. Left/right changes Candidate while Select stays fixed; Up makes Candidate the Select and advances, and Down swaps the pair. Promotion does not tag a photograph.

Click either pane to choose the target for tag, rating, and label commands. The active border identifies that target. Linked Zoom keeps inspection aligned; turn it off to inspect each photo independently. Done or Esc returns to the preceding layout with Select selected.

N opens Survey: the whole current stack, twelve frames per page, or up to six selected photographs. Double-clicking a stack in the grid or filmstrip opens this same whole-stack view. Survey arrows stay within the set.

Hold B to temporarily inspect Select. Outside Compare, it uses the first tagged photograph in the current group. Releasing B restores the previous view.

articles.title: Burst stacks and exposure brackets
articles.body:
Burst stacks keep one capture sequence together. Recorded identifiers and supported Sony sequence counters take priority. When that information is unavailable, Ingest uses a conservative maximum gap between consecutive frames from an identifiable camera, including its serial number. The default gap is two seconds, adjustable in Settings. Missing or uncertain evidence leaves photos separate. Framing changes do not split a recorded burst, and bursts have no 30-frame limit.

Choose stack types

Open Browse by for a compact Sections checklist and Stacks options. Check Day, Camera, Lens, ISO, or Location to create sections; leave all unchecked for a continuous grid. Choose Exposure Brackets, Bursts, or Similar Frames under Stacks. Workspaces can save these viewing choices. Double-click a burst for its whole-frame Survey; C keeps the two-pane Select/Candidate comparison. Previous/Next Burst controls appear while inspecting a burst.

Choose burst keepers

For a burst, P adds the current frame as a keeper without removing existing keepers. Keep Only This Frame is a separate command.

Photo Suggestions shows each burst or set of similar shots as its own section, the suggested photo marked and the reason in the header, and leaves out photos with nothing to compare; ↑ and ↓ move between sets, and nothing is tagged until you choose Tag. It never treats exposure brackets as competing candidates. Sort by Visual appeal orders a folder by the on-device appeal estimate, most appealing first, with photos not yet analyzed last; it is an order to look through, not a rating.

Exposure brackets

A three or five shot bracket is one picture taken several times. Ingest recognizes those sets and shows them as a single cell with a badge, so a card of a hundred brackets looks like twenty pictures instead of a hundred frames.

S expands or collapses the set you are on, ⌥S does all of them. A mark on a collapsed set applies to every frame in it, so tagging the bracket keeps the whole bracket.

Sets are found two ways. Sony writes a flag saying the frames were an auto bracket, which is definitive. Fujifilm does not, so Ingest looks for frames taken a fraction of a second apart with the same aperture and ISO and a clean spread of shutter speeds. Sets of three, five, seven, and nine are recognized, and an incomplete set is still stacked and marked as incomplete rather than quietly hidden.

Correct a stack

If it gets one wrong, fix it. Select frames and combine them into a stack, or uncombine one. Your corrections are remembered for that folder. Exposure stacking can be turned off per folder with ⌥⌘K.

RAW and JPEG pairs

A RAW and JPEG / HEIF pair is handled separately: by default the two files show as one photograph, and marking or copying acts on both. ⌥⌘J turns that off for a folder when you want to see them apart.

articles.title: Filters and saved views
articles.body:
The Filter panel offers All, Tagged, and Untagged, along with ratings, colors, Unmarked, and other filters. Unmarked means no tag, stars, or color. Your saved views remain in a collapsible sidebar section. Clicking the active filter beside the folder name clears it.

The counts update as you mark, which turns culling into something you can see the end of. ⌥Tab steps through the splits.

Set up a filter you like and press ⇧⌘S to save it as your own split. Settings → Browsing → Filters lets you edit one, give it an icon, or hide the built-in ones you never use.

Filters behave: they survive going in and out of the preview, they wrap where you expect, and marking the last photograph out of a view returns you to everything rather than leaving you in an empty room.

articles.title: Overlays
articles.body:
I cycles the information panel: off, the exposure, then everything including the pixel size being displayed. That last part matters, because it tells you whether you are looking at a small preview or the full size image.

KeyOverlay
ICamera, lens, exposure, and what size image is on screen.
⌥DDetail. Turns the image into pure edge contrast, which makes soft frames obvious.
⌥EEdges, drawn in color over the photograph.
⌥AThe focus point the camera recorded, when it recorded one. Sony and Fujifilm both do; Ingest explains when the information is unavailable.
⌥FFace close-ups along the bottom, each cropped at full size so you can check the eyes without zooming.

Subject close-ups and culling analysis run locally using Apple’s Vision framework. Ingest caches face and subject regions, feature prints, and assessment results for inspection and similar-photo grouping. Corrections such as Sharp Enough and Intentional Closed Eyes persist locally. No names or identities are assigned, and analysis is not sent to a server.

Dark, low-contrast, and exposure-bracket frames can be unsuitable for a confident sharpness judgment. Ingest explains uncertainty instead of treating an unavailable assessment as acceptable detail. Use the detail or focus peaking to inspect the photograph yourself.

Focus Peaking (⌥E) overlays green edge highlights while preserving the original color and brightness. It is not a complete map of focused areas: low-contrast detail can be sharp without a highlight. Toggle it off and inspect the original at 100% before deciding.

articles.title: Crop and straighten
articles.body: Select a writable photo and choose Crop & Straighten in Preview, the photo context menu, or ⌘K. Drag a frame corner to crop, drag inside to reposition, choose an aspect ratio, and use Straighten to adjust the angle. Save records reversible crop geometry; Cancel discards the draft. Copy Crop and Paste Crop to Selection reuse a composition after reviewing the affected photos.

articles.title: Client pick lists
articles.body:
1. Open the relevant folder or Photos collection and confirm the photos currently available for review.
  2. Find Select from Pick List… in ⌘K.
  3. Choose Filenames / relative paths or Displayed image numbers. Paste the list, or choose Load File… for a saved text list.
  4. Review matched, missing, and ambiguous entries. Choose Select Matches to select uniquely matched photos.

Image numbers refer to the current displayed review order, not necessarily the numeric part of a camera filename. Use filenames or relative paths when order may have changed. Matching creates a selection; it does not automatically tag, export, or send the photos.

Ingest decision files are a separate use of the same sheet. Their review shows current and proposed tags, ratings, labels, and reviewed state before Apply Decisions. Protected decisions are skipped.

articles.title: RAW histogram and preview comparison
articles.body:
Choose the sensor histogram

The inspector starts with a tone histogram of the displayed preview. In Settings → Sidebar Information, choose the sensor histogram for supported RAW files. Supported Bayer and X-Trans sensor data, including DNG files with these mosaics, is read directly with black levels subtracted. White balance, demosaic, and rendering tone curves do not affect this histogram.

Read channels and scale

RGB curves remain visible by default. Use Combined / RGB / R / G / B to combine curves or isolate a channel. An individual RAW channel shows its headroom and clipped percentage. Both green photosite populations are combined, and channels are normalized so green does not dominate simply because the sensor contains more green photosites.

Use Log (stops) / Linear to change the RAW scale (also available by right-clicking). The default runs from −16 stops to the white level at 0; its midpoint is −8 stops, only 0.39% of sensor saturation. JPEG charts use rendered tone values from 0 to 255, so horizontal positions in the two charts are not directly comparable. White balance and tone processing can make the JPEG reach white before the sensor saturates. Saturated values appear in a separate area at the right edge.

Highlight headroom

Highlight headroom measures the brightest channel’s 99.9th percentile against the camera/file white level, reducing the effect of a few hot pixels. Once 0.1% of any channel clips, the line changes to Clipped: 2.4%, for example. This percentage describes the channel with the highest clipped proportion, not a demosaiced pixel count. Clipping below the threshold still appears at the chart’s right edge. An entirely black signal shows “Headroom unavailable.” The measurement covers the active sensor area, independent of display crops.

JPEG and RAW previews

JPEG selects a linear histogram of the paired JPEG, or the largest readable embedded JPEG when no readable JPEG companion exists. The source label’s tooltip identifies which file or preview is used. JPEG histograms do not report RAW highlight headroom.

Render RAW Preview, below the main photo or in the Command Palette, renders only the selected photo. The existing image stays visible while it loads. The photographic rendering includes camera white balance; it remains separate from the unrendered sensor histogram. Choose Show JPEG Preview to return.

Show clipping

Enable Show clipping on image to mark clipped regions for the selected channels and histogram source. RAW uses sensor saturation; JPEG uses full-resolution rendered values at 255. Each marker can cover several photosites so small clipped areas remain visible when zoomed out. Markers follow zoom, pan, orientation, and supported display crops. Camera JPEG crops or lens corrections can shift alignment with sensor regions. The overlay label identifies its source, including JPEG fallback. This display does not change exposure or the image file.

Compare RAW and JPEG

Compare RAW and JPEG in the command palette opens the same photo’s labeled RAW and JPEG previews side by side, with linked zoom and pan and full-resolution loading for 100% inspection. The RAW histogram remains available in the inspector. Close Comparison returns to the single preview. Navigating to another photo returns to ordinary preview loading. This differs from C, which compares multiple photographs.

Fallbacks and processing

If RAW data cannot be read, Ingest labels the fallback JPEG histogram and explains: “Couldn't read raw data for this file. Showing the JPEG histogram instead.” If no JPEG can be read, the module shows an unavailable state. Other rendered formats retain their own source labels. Unsupported sensor layouts and RAW compression variants use this fallback.

Calculation runs in the background and is cached by file revision. Loading holds the chart’s space; results fade in when ready. RAW rendering and analysis pause during ingest. These controls inspect exposure and rendering; they do not adjust exposure or assign ratings.

articles.title: Metadata Assist
articles.body:
Edit Metadata… opens Metadata Assist. Choose Edit Individual Fields… inside it for the detailed field editor. Use Changes returns that draft to the review panel; only Apply applies the reviewed changes.

Choose fields

⌘’ opens Metadata Assist for selected photos or the current import. Choose Keywords, Caption, or Location to begin, or type ; to see your field options, pick one (a fragment like ;lo narrows the list), then Tab to take it and fill the value or search for a place. Separate keywords with commas.

;
;lo
;capt

Review changes

Recognized fields appear immediately in the review panel. Correct a value, add another field, inspect existing values, or change its operation. Keywords append by default; most other fields begin with Replace. Fill Empty and other operations depend on the field. Unrecognized input and caption-code errors remain visible until resolved.

Keyword completion and recent details

Previously applied or staged values are remembered locally. Type a prefix and press Tab to fill the highlighted suggestion; arrow keys choose another result and Escape dismisses suggestions. Keywords complete individually after commas and also use Ingest’s existing keyword history. Caption and other field histories stay separate.

Recent values recalls an individual field or map location; each field’s options menu also lists recent values. Use Last Details replaces the current review draft with the last applied set. It does not apply anything. Canceled and failed drafts do not enter history; the last 20 distinct values per field and 20 map locations are kept locally.

Place names and map pins

A typed Location supplies IPTC place text and leaves GPS unchanged. Type ;loc, choose Map Location, and press Return to search Apple Maps. Search saved places or addresses, or paste coordinates or an Apple Maps coordinate link.

Select a result to review its pin; typing focus returns to the writing area. Save Location… stores a named place for reuse across the location pickers, including Apple Photos. Saved places work offline. Right-click a saved result to remove it. Saving a location does not write to photos.

Work through a selection

With one photo selected, Previous and Next browse the current order while keeping separate unsaved drafts. For a multiple selection, choose Edit Individually to work through that selection, or Edit Together to return to its batch draft. Apply saves and keeps Assist open; Apply & Next saves and advances only after success. Close discards unapplied drafts. When opened from Import Settings, Metadata Assist stages details for imported copies.

Prepare an import

Stage client, event, location, and shoot date for naming and folder templates. Use for Import updates the plan; copying is still a separate action. Metadata is written to verified destination copies. Shoot date does not rewrite capture timestamps. Projects retain shared details across cards; otherwise choose Keep details for the next card. Explicit per-photo edits take precedence.

Caption codes and copying

Workspace caption codes expand short codes into known text, using UTF-8 tab-separated files and normally the = delimiter. ⇧⌘C copies selected metadata groups; ⇧⌘V pastes those groups for the current selection. Copy choices are remembered per workspace.

Apply or discard

Add details. Review. Apply. Typing alone writes nothing. Metadata Assist does not invent captions or infer instructions from prose. Cancel discards the draft. Its built-in How to use Metadata Assist guide provides examples.

Q retains the earlier Quick Entry syntax inside the same reviewed editor. See the syntax reference.

articles.title: Metadata
articles.body:
Photo Info keeps Caption, Keywords, and Location close at hand. Its menu opens the full IPTC editor when you need specialized fields. Choose and reorder sidebar fields in Settings → Sidebar Information. Ingest writes supported rendered files directly and uses XMP sidecars for proprietary RAW files. Export a JPEG with metadata and GPS included for apps such as Apple Photos that may not read RAW sidecars.

Use Suggest… beside Caption or Keywords for on-device Apple Intelligence suggestions on supported macOS 27 systems. Review each photo, edit the suggested text, and choose what to save. Nothing is written until you approve.

Location accepts address/place search, decimal latitude and longitude, an Apple Maps link containing coordinates, or just city and state. Camera location describes where you stood and can set the GPS used by map apps. Place in the photo describes the subject location; photographing a skyline from across a river is one example where they differ. Saving only place names leaves GPS unchanged.

Open the inspector with ⌘I. K opens Keywords. ⇧C goes to the caption. ⇧K takes back the keywords you just added, which is the one you will want after applying the wrong thing to forty photographs.

Every write is checked. Ingest keeps the tool's backup of the file until it has read the file back and confirmed the new value, then removes the backup. If the read back does not match, the original is put back. That is why writing metadata to a hundred files takes a moment.

Never to a card. Camera originals are never modified. Set metadata in the ingest flow to apply it to verified destination copies.

articles.title: GPS and descriptive locations
articles.body:
Map coordinates and descriptive place names serve different purposes. In Metadata Assist, type ;loc, choose Map Location, and press Return. Search through Apple Maps, choose a result, and review its pin before applying GPS coordinates.

Descriptive IPTC fields such as city, state, country, and the place shown in the photo are separate. Enter and review those fields when you want searchable place text. Saving place names alone does not change GPS. A saved location makes a place reusable; saving it does not itself edit photographs.

For files and folders, the separate job Location command is available with ⌘L. Review its selected location, fields, and target scope before applying. ⇧⌘L removes location information from the chosen targets. Metadata on a card is staged for imported copies.

Compatible apps read supported saved fields from image files or XMP sidecars. Apple Photos may need a JPEG export with metadata and GPS included when it does not read a RAW sidecar. Troubleshoot missing metadata.

Address searches send your query to Apple. Saved places can be reused offline. Location privacy →

articles.title: Metadata templates
articles.body:
A metadata template stores reusable field operations, such as filling empty Creator and Copyright fields or adding keywords. M opens one Apply Metadata Template sheet with template selection, any required answers, a resolved preview, and Apply. New Template and Edit Copy return to that selection. Editing a copy leaves the shared original unchanged.

The preview shows each field’s operation, existing value, and resulting value. Clear, unchanged, and mixed values are identified explicitly. Keywords can add to existing values, and Fill Empty preserves values already present. Missing required answers must be completed before applying.

Templates can use naming tokens and answers from workspace questions. Preview resolves them using the selected photographs. Changes to the template, inputs, or photo selection require an updated preview.

Select a template in Import Settings or the workspace’s Metadata section to apply it to verified destination copies. Fields shown during import controls the visible editing fields only; it does not choose a template or change what the template writes.

articles.title: Camera and lens details for film scans
articles.body:
Choose Camera & Lens… in Metadata Assist. Pick saved equipment from My Gear, search the offline camera/lens catalog, or save a custom make and model. Enter known aperture, shutter speed, ISO, and focal length; leave unknown details blank. Shutter speed accepts a fraction such as 1/125 or seconds.

Fill missing values preserves recorded metadata. Choose Replace recorded values when the scan describes the scanner instead of the taking camera. Review Details returns to Metadata Assist before Apply. JPEG/TIFF edits and RAW sidecars use verification and Undo. During ingest, the details go to verified copies. My Gear is saved on this Mac and does not yet sync with Ingest Field.

articles.title: Fujifilm recipes
articles.body:
When browsing files and folders, select a Fujifilm JPEG to see Fujifilm Recipe below Location in Photo Info. Its collapsed heading shows the detected film simulation. Expand it to read the camera’s recorded settings or saved notes. Copy, Export, Edit, and the keyword action sit above the details. Choose Edit to change the text; Save, Cancel, and Use Camera Settings stay above the editor. JPEG companions in RAW + JPEG pairs work too.

If the photo already has saved notes, Ingest displays them as written. Otherwise, it prepares an unsaved draft from the recognized simulation and available white balance, tone, color, grain, and other settings. It leaves missing settings out and does not guess unknown simulations or custom recipe names.

Edit or replace the entire text, then choose Save to keep it with the JPEG. Cancel restores saved notes or the detected camera settings. Use Camera Settings restores the detected recipe while editing. Viewing a recipe does not write metadata. Recipe notes share the Instructions field with the full metadata editor. On a card, Save opens a short dialog to queue the notes for after ingest.

Copy copies the text currently shown. Export saves it as a .txt or .md file, including unsaved edits. These are files for sharing and reference, not profiles that can be loaded onto a camera.

Add “Provia” to Keywords names the simulation it will add. The button changes to a checkmark and confirmation when the keyword is present. Existing keywords stay in place and duplicates are avoided. With multiple photos selected, each qualifying JPEG gets its own simulation keyword; select one qualifying JPEG to edit recipe text. Recipe saves and simulation keywords affect only JPEGs, including in RAW + JPEG pairs.

On a card, recipe saves and simulation keywords are queued only after you confirm the dialog. Choose Don’t show again to skip future card recipe confirmations. Turn them back on with Confirm card recipe changes in Settings → Sidebar Information → Fujifilm Recipe.

Queued changes are kept on your Mac, survive restarting Ingest, and apply to verified JPEG copies at both destinations after the ingest preset. Undo removes a queued change. Card originals and RAW companions stay untouched; Copy and Export work immediately. A queued change remains associated with its source photo for subsequent ingests until you undo it.

Use Settings → Sidebar Information to hide or reorder the section.

articles.title: Adjust capture time across cameras
articles.body:
Use Adjust Capture Time… in ⌘K, or press ⌥⌘T while browsing files. The sheet lists detected cameras, distinguishing serial numbers when available, and the photo count for each.

  1. Compare photographs of the same clock or event to work out each camera’s correction.
  2. Enter a signed offset beside that camera: +1h, -90s, or +2m30s. Leave a camera at zero to keep its times.
  3. Review the camera counts and the number of files on the write button before applying.

The scope is all loaded photos for each camera with a nonzero offset, not only your selection. Open the intended folder scope first. This is a metadata write for writable files; import card originals before adjusting them. The job’s Shoot date used in naming is separate and does not rewrite capture timestamps.

articles.title: Destinations
articles.body:
Favorites give you quick access to folders you use often. Add to Favorites is available in the menu and command palette; ⌃⌘1 through ⌃⌘9 open the first nine favorites. Find them by name in ⌘K as well. Ingest destinations and routing are saved with the workspace.

An ingest can write to two destinations at once. The second copy is made from the first one after it has been verified, and it is checked the same way.

The active workspace supplies import defaults. Open Import… to review or adjust a single job. Edit the Import Folders and Import File Names sections in Settings → Workspaces to save destinations, naming, and routing for reuse.

Keep archive organization separate

The workspace’s Organize section saves a separate destination and naming setup. Rename in Place changes filenames only and ignores that destination and folder structure.

articles.title: Renaming
articles.body:
Type names and insert variables

In Import File Names or the separate Organize setup, type ordinary text and choose Insert Variable. Type { to find a variable directly; choose a suggestion with Return. Variables appear as readable pieces in the same text field. Choose your own spaces and separators.

Advanced pattern exposes the same pattern as text. Custom Import settings use this editor too. Check the resolved preview before applying names.

Choose the right date

Import Date uses the import’s date, so photos taken over several days can share one import folder. Today’s Date uses the task’s date. Capture Date uses the photograph’s date; a containing folder uses the earliest date in the selection. See the date reference for exact tokens and fallback behavior.

Renaming happens during an ingest, or in place afterwards with ⌘R. ⌥⌘R re-sequences what is on screen, which is how you close the gaps in the numbering after throwing half a shoot away.

Every rename records the original filename inside the file, so Undo Rename can put the old names back later, even in a folder you opened fresh.

Set Photo Number options

Insert Photo Number, then open Photo Number options… to choose the starting number and digit width. One digit means no padding; larger widths add leading zeros. Photo Number continues across imports, with a project keeping its own count. The separate photo-number-in-this-import variable starts within the current import. Review the resolved example before copying.

Choose What do the variables mean? for definitions. Under Ask when importing, select a question or add New Question…. Only questions used by your names or metadata template appear at import.

articles.title: Import and verify copies
articles.body:
⌘G or Import… opens Import Settings from Browse, with settings on the left and photo scope and output preview on the right. Choose a card, folder, or archive; the active workspace supplies the saved destination, names, metadata, and routing. Review the destination preview before starting.

Choose the photos

Photos to import offers All, Tagged, Untagged, and Selected. Opening Import Settings starts at Selected when photos are selected, otherwise All. Display filters do not choose this scope, and an empty scope does not fall back to All. A project retains shared job details; a shoot identifies a session that may span several cards. New sources start with No project. Review the scope count and output paths every time.

Settings cover the workspace and project, shoot details, photo groups, destinations, filenames, metadata, files, and after-import actions. The preview shows the chosen photos and final output paths. Changes for one import do not require a new workspace. Invalid destination text cannot replace a committed folder; Return selects the folder without starting the transfer.

Assign photo groups

Name Photo Groups such as Cocktail Hour, Speeches, and Late Night, then assign photos by drag-and-drop or the searchable assignment sheet. RAW/JPEG partners stay together. Group names, numbers, and optional keywords do not require group folders. Turn on Create a subfolder for each group separately if wanted. When names or folders require a group, Assign Remaining Photos resolves the unassigned list before import.

Review the plan

Open Preview Metadata Changes to see the actual operations and resulting values. Import freezes the reviewed photo IDs, destinations, filenames, group allocations, metadata changes, and action targets. Relevant changes or source-file edits require preparation again.

Copy and verify

Click Import after reviewing the plan. Then:

  • Each file is copied to a temporary name and flushed to disk.
  • The copy is read back and compared to the source. If they differ, that file is not published and the ingest says so.
  • The verified copy is given its real name, in a way that cannot overwrite an existing file even if one appeared a moment ago.
  • A second destination is copied from the first and checked the same way.
  • Metadata and marks are written to the copies.
  • A record of the job is saved, so Ingest can tell you later which photographs from this card you have already taken.
  • After copying, metadata processing, receipt persistence, and required actions succeed, explicit card-cleanup choices run. For RAW-only imports, Delete copied files also removes intentionally excluded JPEG/HEIF twins after their RAW verifies at every destination. Leave the card alone preserves both.

Follow progress or keep browsing

Import Progress opens automatically. Separate bars show copying and verification, with the current file and destination. Later stages show their current activity. Choose Continue Browsing to return to your photos while the import runs, then reopen progress from the photo-count/activity control. Import Complete or Import Needs Attention shows the result.

The progress display shows copied files and verified, published files separately. Each destination gets a completion check only when it holds every planned file. If an ingest stops early, the receipt identifies what remains only on the card and offers a deliberate retry.

Continue across cards

Canceling keeps verified copies. Named-group allocations remain reserved so retries retain their names; gaps after a partial failure are possible. The same shoot continues numbering across cards, while a new shoot starts fresh. Renaming or reordering a group does not rename files already imported.

Finish or retry

Completion cards offer Browse in Ingest and Reveal in Finder. Details identify incomplete work and skipped or failed actions. Retrying unfinished actions leaves successful actions alone; automatic card cleanup does not run when required work failed.

articles.title: After-import actions, Lightroom, and automation
articles.body:
An action is a list of steps that opens files in an app, reveals them in Finder, sends them to Apple Photos, copies them elsewhere, or runs a Shortcut or script. In the workspace’s After Import section, add ordered actions and choose Photos for this action independently for each. For example, import All and open only Tagged copies in Lightroom.

They are built in Settings → Automation, with a button that runs one on the current selection so you can test it without waiting for a card. The detail, including what a script gets handed, is on the automation page.

Import everything; open only tagged copies

  1. Set Photos to import to All.
  2. In the workspace’s After Import section, add an action that opens files in your chosen editor.
  3. Set Photos for this action to Tagged. Review that action’s count independently of the import count.
  4. Start the reviewed import. The action works on the imported copies within its own scope.

Opening files in Lightroom hands them to that app; it is not a promise that Lightroom silently completes its catalog import. Use the completion details to review skipped or failed actions. Troubleshoot after-import actions →

articles.title: Organize
articles.body:
Choose the operation

The inspector follows Grouping, Destination, Filenames, and Destination Preview. When you choose the workspace as the starting setup, its Organize section supplies the destination, folder structure, and filenames. Enable full paths when useful, review example filenames, then use Review Changes… to confirm the proposed operation before execution.

Choose File → Organize… in Browse, or find Organize in the photo context menu or Command Palette. It opens a separate, resizable window. Browse keeps its selection, filter, and scroll position behind it.

Organize resumes the folder’s saved draft when available. Set its photo scope to All, Selected, or Filtered and choose whether to include subfolders. For a new task, explicitly choose Copy, Move, or Rename in Place before Continue becomes available. Then add grouping levels or a recipe. Opening the editor does not change files. Copy Import Naming & Folder Structure in workspace settings copies those choices once; later Import edits do not change Organize.

Set destinations and names

Rename in Place changes filenames only; saved destinations and folder structures are not applied. Import Date is unavailable for existing photos. Use Today’s Date or Capture Date instead.

Add or change grouping levels, make your own groups, and move photos between them. Grouping choices do not change the original files. Review the proposed filenames and destinations before applying Copy, Move, or Rename. Existing files are preserved; conflicts must be resolved before applying changes. Memory cards must be ingested first.

Resume or start over

Once you edit your choices or accept a new setup, Ingest saves that work for the folder. Returning shows Resumed saved setup and its last-edited date. Start Over opens the setup chooser again; applying a new setup can be undone and keeps the history needed to recover earlier file operations.

Save a recipe to reuse grouping and naming choices with another folder. Drafts and recipes stay on your Mac; recipes can travel with a settings export.

After reconnecting a drive

Reopen the original source to recover its tags, ratings, and saved Organize draft. Check any interrupted import separately. Resume work after reconnecting →

articles.title: Send to Decks
articles.body:
Select still photos in Browse or Apple Photos and choose File → Send to Decks…, search for it in ⌘K, use the photo or group context menu, or press ⇧⌘E. Photos are sent in visible order. Video selections are not supported.

Choose Original files or JPEG copies. JPEG copies offer dimensions, quality, file-size, sharpening, and metadata choices, with a prepared count and size before sending. Some RAW conversions use an embedded preview or companion JPEG and may contain less detail; the sheet explains this before sending.

Open in Decks for Mac uses an installed compatible Mac app. Send via iCloud makes the transfer available in Incoming Photos in Decks on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. AirDrop or Share… uses the system sharing sheet. Decks waits for you to choose New Project or Existing Project; Later keeps the transfer in Incoming Photos.

iCloud transfers require iCloud sign-in and a compatible Decks version. Ingest keeps a saved transfer queue with status, retry, and completion checks. This is an explicit photo transfer, separate from Ingest workspace settings. Transfer storage and privacy →

The transfer contains independent photo copies with integrity checks. Decks retains its own media, so moving the originals later does not break the received project. Cloud-only Apple Photos images may need downloading before the transfer is ready. Receiving requires a Decks version that supports Ingest handoffs.

Starting with Ingest 0.9.6, the built-in Social Export editor is removed. Ordinary JPEG export and crop controls remain in Ingest. Existing original photos, previous exports, and saved photo data are preserved; this change does not automatically convert old Social Export projects into Decks projects.

Learn about Decks →

articles.title: Share photos and folders through Messages or Email
articles.body:
Share selected photos

  1. Select the photos you want to share.
  2. Open the photo context menu or press ⌘K and choose Send Photos via Messages… or Send Photos via Email….
  3. Check the file count and total size. For multiple files, choose Attach Files or Create ZIP. A single file offers Continue.
  4. Review the draft in Messages or your email app, add recipients, and send it there.

Ingest opens a draft; it does not send the message. File-based sharing uses the selected visible photos’ primary files in their existing formats. It does not automatically turn RAW files into JPEGs or attach XMP sidecars.

Share a folder

Use the folder’s context menu, or find Send Folder via Messages… or Send Folder via Email… in the Command Palette. Folder sharing includes photos and videos independently of the grid’s filter or selection.

An ordinary folder includes directly contained media. Cards, volume roots, and the current folder with subfolders enabled include nested media too. Hidden files, symbolic links, unrelated files, and sidecars are excluded. Check the count before continuing.

Share from Apple Photos

Select still images and use the photo sharing commands. Ingest prepares rendered copies that preserve Photos edits. This path does not support Apple Photos video sharing.

If a sharing draft does not open →

articles.title: Preview RAW photos with saved Adobe edits
articles.body:
Use an Adobe-rendered preview to see saved edits while browsing RAW files. Adobe DNG Converter must be installed on your Mac.

Show the saved edits

  1. Select a RAW photo from a card or folder.
  2. Press ⌘K and choose Preview with Adobe Edits.
  3. Wait for the preview to render. If prompted, use Choose Converter… to select your Adobe DNG Converter installation.

Ingest uses settings saved in the file or its companion XMP/ACR data. Edits stored only inside a Lightroom catalog are not included; save the edits to the file or sidecar in your Adobe app first. Ingest creates a cached preview without rewriting the original RAW.

Refresh or return to the camera preview

Run Preview with Adobe Edits again after saving new edits. Choose Show Camera Preview to return to the camera’s embedded preview. Adobe previews are separate from the sensor-based RAW histogram.

Troubleshoot missing or outdated previews →

articles.title: What you need
articles.body:
Requires macOS 15 Sequoia or later and a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer). Intel Macs are not supported.

  • Apple Intelligence is optional. Text-based metadata assistance requires macOS 26 or later; suggestions generated from photographs require macOS 27.
  • Apple Photos: Editing captions, keywords, and native star ratings requires macOS 27. Other browsing and review features work on earlier supported versions.

To check your Mac, choose Apple menu → About This Mac. To install, open the disk image and drag Ingest to Applications.

articles.title: Cameras and files it reads
articles.body:
Ingest prefers an embedded camera preview or a paired JPEG / HEIF image. When a file needs RAW rendering, that slower first preview is handled separately and cached. Camera model and recording mode affect preview availability.

FileWhat happens
Sony .ARWUses available embedded previews, choosing the size needed for the current view.
Fujifilm .RAFReads the embedded JPEG where available.
.JPG and .JPEGReads the image and available embedded previews.
.HEIC, .HEIF, and .HIFOpens and browses.
.MP4 and .MOVBrowses and plays, with a poster frame in the grid. Sony clip sidecars travel with the file when you ingest.
Canon .CR2, .CR3; Nikon .NEF, .NRWEmbedded previews and metadata, including tested Canon CR3 files with HEIF previews.
Hasselblad .3FR, camera-origin .FFFEmbedded previews where available, with rendering fallback for files that need it. Scanner files and specialized multishot reconstruction are excluded.
Panasonic / Lumix .RW2; OM System / Olympus .ORFPreview and metadata support for tested camera samples.
Ricoh / Pentax .DNG, .PEF; Leica .DNG, .RWL, .RW2Preview and metadata support for tested camera samples.

Coverage is based on representative real camera files, not every recording mode. The sampled Nikon Z8 compression mode works through its embedded preview but fails in bundled LibRaw rendering. Native rendering succeeded on macOS 27; macOS 15 runtime remains unverified. Phase One, Sigma, scanner files, and specialized multishot reconstruction are outside this release.

XMP companions belong to their RAW photo and travel with it during file operations. Ambiguous companion groups remain separate.

Files that are never treated as photographs: sidecars such as .XMP and .THM, camera database and index files, and anything beginning with a dot.

articles.title: The first hour
articles.body:
The keys are the part worth learning, and there is a way to practice them that cannot hurt anything. Choose Help, then Open Practice Folder. Ingest builds about thirty throwaway images and opens them, and the status bar tells you which keys to try. Nothing in that folder matters, so tag, rate, label, and undo as roughly as you like.

Press ? at any time for the shortcut sheet, or ⌘K to search every command by name. Tap and release ⌘, then press and hold it again to see contextual shortcuts. The complete list lives on the shortcuts page, and the Getting started guide walks one card from insert to finished folder.

articles.title: Updates
articles.body:
Choose Ingest, then Check for Updates. Automatic checking is off until you turn it on in Settings, General. An update is only installed if it carries a signature made with my key.

What each version changed is in the release notes. Update checks omit hardware profiling; the host receives normal connection information. The privacy page says exactly what does and does not leave the machine.

articles.title: Coming from Photo Mechanic
articles.body:
The habits carry over. T tags, the arrow keys move, ⌘G is ingest, and {seqn} is the saved sequence counter. The naming reference lists supported brace tokens; check your existing patterns against it.

Three differences worth knowing. Marking keys do not advance by default, and you can turn advancing on in Settings → Browsing. Tags are a simple on/off flag, independent of ratings and colors. The Filter panel offers All, Tagged, and Untagged, and the active filter can be cleared from the folder header. And stars and color labels use the Lightroom keys, 1 to 5 and 6 to 9, saved in supported files or XMP sidecars so compatible editing apps can read them.

Settings, Shortcuts lists every command. Click a shortcut or focus it with Tab and press Return to record a new one. Navigation keys and standard Mac editing shortcuts stay fixed; Settings explains any conflict.

articles.title: Memory cards
articles.body:
Insert a card and it appears in the sources list with its name and free space. By default Ingest opens it for you. That is a setting in Settings → Transfers, if you would rather it just sat in the list.

Reviewing does not change your card originals. Ratings, keywords, renaming, and Finder tags are applied to copies, not to files on the card. Source files are deleted only when you explicitly request it after copies have been verified at every destination. That holds however you opened the card, including when you open a folder that happens to live on one. Metadata you add while culling is remembered and applied to the copies during ingest.

If a card does not appear, check that it is mounted in Finder. Ingest looks for a DCIM folder to recognize a volume as a card. A card formatted by something other than a camera may not have one, in which case open it with ⌘O as an ordinary folder.

To eject, press ⌘E. Ingest closes everything it has open on the card first, so eject does not fail with a file in use. If macOS still refuses, another app is holding the card. Pulling a card without ejecting does not crash Ingest. It notices and closes the source.

After reconnecting a drive

Reopen the original source to recover its tags, ratings, and saved Organize draft. Check any interrupted import separately. Resume work after reconnecting →

articles.title: Thumbnails are slow or missing
articles.body:
Preview speed depends on the camera format, available embedded image, storage, and connection. If browsing is slow, try a local copy to distinguish file-rendering work from a slow card reader, network volume, or file provider.

Thumbnails that are expensive to build are cached on disk, under 2 GB, and cleared from Settings, Advanced. Clearing the cache is safe and never touches a photograph.

A photograph with no thumbnail at all is usually a raw format Ingest cannot read yet. See cameras and files it reads.

Adobe preview is unavailable

Select a RAW photo from a card or folder, then run Preview with Adobe Edits. Install Adobe DNG Converter or use Choose Converter… to locate it. If conversion fails for your camera, use Get Latest Converter… in the preview notice and try again.

Adobe edits are missing or outdated

Save the edits to the photo or its sidecar in your Adobe app; Lightroom catalog-only edits are not visible to Ingest. Run Preview with Adobe Edits again to refresh. Show Camera Preview returns to the embedded camera image. Adobe preview guide →

articles.title: Review, focus peaking, or eye results look wrong
articles.body:
Eye and sharpness assessments are assistance, not final decisions. Inspect the face or detail at a useful zoom and check the original photo. Low-contrast detail can be sharp without a focus-peaking highlight. Uncertain face results need your judgment.

Review uses a fixed queue: marking a photograph does not remove it from that queue. Browse filters are separate. If expected photos are missing, check the active filter, collapsed stacks, and Subfolders.

Keys depend on context. F enters Focus Mode in file Browse, while Photos browsing uses F for Favorite. A text field can also consume typing. Use ⌘K to find the action and read why it is unavailable. Review guide · Shortcut contexts.

articles.title: A client pick list has missing or ambiguous matches
articles.body:
Open the intended folder or Photos collection first. Choose the correct match mode: Filenames / relative paths or Displayed image numbers. Numbers refer to the current displayed review order; they are not automatically camera filename suffixes.

Use a relative path to distinguish repeated filenames in different folders, or narrow the collection. Review the missing and ambiguous counts before Select Matches. Selecting matches does not apply ratings or tags. Pick-list instructions →

articles.title: Lightroom or Photos does not show my keywords
articles.body:
Ingest writes metadata directly into supported rendered files and uses XMP sidecars for proprietary RAW files. Apple Photos may not read RAW sidecars. Export a JPEG with metadata and GPS included, then send that JPEG to Photos when those fields need to travel with the image. Native Photos edits are available separately in the Photos workspace, with caption, keyword, and rating writes requiring macOS 27.

Two things to check first. Metadata is never written to a card, so if you added keywords while culling, they are applied to the copies during ingest and you should look at the copies. And ratings and labels are written in the background a couple of seconds after you stop pressing keys, so a file read the instant you rated it may not have caught up.

The writing is done by ExifTool, which is included in the app. Ingest keeps ExifTool's backup of each file until it has read the file back and confirmed the write, then removes it. If the read back does not match, the original is put back.

If Settings, Advanced reports that the metadata tool is not ready, turn Use the built-in exiftool back on. The built-in copy runs with the Perl that ships with macOS. If a future macOS removes Perl, that switch and a copy installed with Homebrew are the way back.

articles.title: I entered a location, but there is no map pin
articles.body:
Descriptive city, state, country, and place names are different from GPS coordinates. In Metadata Assist, type ;loc, choose Map Location, and press Return. Search Apple Maps, select a result, review its pin, and apply it to the intended photos.

When checking another app, open the edited copies, not card originals. Apple Photos may not read a RAW XMP sidecar; export a JPEG with metadata and GPS included if those fields must travel. GPS and descriptive locations →

articles.title: Fujifilm Recipe is missing or incomplete
articles.body:
Select one supported Fujifilm JPEG, or a RAW + JPEG pair with a qualifying JPEG companion. The recipe section uses recorded JPEG camera settings; a RAW file alone does not qualify for this tool. Check Settings → Sidebar Information if the section is hidden.

Missing settings are omitted. Ingest does not guess a custom recipe name. Previously saved notes can differ from the detected settings; Use Camera Settings restores the detected draft while editing. Copy and Export produce reference text, not a camera-installable profile. Fujifilm recipe guide →

articles.title: My workspace or filenames are not right
articles.body:
1. Confirm the active workspace in the window toolbar. Open at Launch is a separate choice.
  2. Open its setup and check required questions, the receiving folder, and Import File Names. New workspaces keep original filenames until you change that choice.
  3. Connect an external destination. If its drive was renamed, reselect the folder.
  4. Use Review & Save to inspect the examples, save the workspace, then check the actual output paths in Import Settings.

For continuing group numbers, choose the same shoot across cards. A new shoot starts fresh; failed or partial imports may leave reserved-number gaps. Workspace Builder · Naming reference.

Import and Organize use different settings

Check the section for the task you are running. Import Folders and Import File Names do not configure Organize. An existing folder may resume its saved Organize draft; choose Start Over to choose a fresh setup.

The folder date is unexpected

Import Date keeps a multi-day selection in one import-date folder. Capture Date uses the earliest photo date for a containing folder. Organize cannot use Import Date; replace it with Today’s Date or Capture Date.

A starter preview did not change my workspace

Expanding Events, Headshots, or Real Estate shows a preview. Choose its Use button to apply it, then review and save the workspace.

A question is missing at import

Insert its answer into a folder name, filename, or metadata template. Unused questions are not asked. Check You’ll be asked at import in the builder. Questions no longer have a separate builder step.

Where are Photo Groups?

Configure Photo Groups in Import Settings. They are no longer a Workspace Builder section. Keep original filenames if you do not need group-based naming.

articles.title: A copy did not finish
articles.body:
Ingest copies to a temporary name, flushes it to disk, reads the copy back, compares it to the source, and only then gives it its real name. Nothing is ever overwritten. If something goes wrong part way, the files that were already copied and verified are kept and the rest are not, and the receipt records what happened.

The Import button is dim
The reason is printed beside it. The usual ones are no destination chosen, an empty All, Tagged, or Selected scope, a template that will not parse, or two photographs that would end up with the same name.
Names collide
Ingest refuses rather than quietly adding a suffix. Add {seqn} or {seq} to the template so every name is different. See collisions.
Not enough space
The import plan checks free space before it starts and tells you, rather than filling the disk and failing at photograph two hundred.
Deleting from the card
Keep Leave the card alone to preserve originals. If you choose Delete copied files, copies must verify at every destination. In a RAW-only import, cleanup also removes the intentionally excluded JPEG/HEIF twin after its RAW verifies. Changed, failed, or protected files are retained. Delete everything asks for confirmation and is not remembered for next time.

Find import progress

Import Progress opens automatically. Continue Browsing dismisses the panel without stopping the import. Use the photo-count/activity control to reopen it. Copy and verification are separate stages; later activity can continue after both bars finish. Check Import Complete or Import Needs Attention before disconnecting a drive.

articles.title: Backup strategy
articles.body:
Use a separate physical drive for Photo Backup. Ingest’s second verified copy is one part of a backup workflow: arrange off-site protection and editor/catalog backups separately.

A Lightroom catalog backup does not back up your original photographs. See 3-2-1 backup guidance for keeping originals safe across media and locations.

Project folders that separate source photographs from outputs are an approach also used by Capture One Sessions. They are not mandatory standards.

articles.title: Lightroom, a Shortcut, or an after-import action did not run
articles.body:
1. Check the completion details for skipped or failed actions.
  2. Check each action’s Photos for this action scope. Importing All does not mean an action set to Tagged receives every file.
  3. Confirm the chosen app, Shortcut, or script is available on this Mac, and review any permission prompt.
  4. Retry unfinished actions from the result when offered. Successful actions are left alone.

Open an action in Settings → Automation and test it on a small disposable selection when appropriate. Opening files in an editor and importing them into that editor’s catalog are separate steps. After-import workflow · Automation reference.

articles.title: Permission prompts
articles.body:
macOS asks before an app reads a removable volume. Allow it, or Ingest cannot see your cards. If you dismissed it, the switch is in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Files and Folders.

Connecting to Apple Photos or sending files to it requests Photos read/write permission. Ingest uses your System Photo Library, not an arbitrary library file. If Connect did nothing in an older beta, update to the current release and try again. If access was denied, choose Open Photos Privacy Settings, enable Ingest, and return to the app. Settings → General controls Apple Photos integration for the app, and each workspace has its own switch. Both must be on. Turning integration off hides Photos controls and stops observation; it preserves your saved state. An action that runs a Shortcut asks for permission to control Shortcuts when needed.

articles.title: Apple Photos availability
articles.body: Native caption, keyword, and rating edits require macOS 27. Earlier supported versions keep Photos ratings local and provide native favorites, dates, and locations. Cloud-only media needs a working connection to Apple Photos. Offline iCloud transfers, switching System Photo Libraries, and playback across all Live Photo and video formats remain beta validation areas. Use Import History to review interrupted or uncertain imports before retrying.

articles.title: Photos have not appeared in Decks
articles.body:
Send to Decks works with selected still photos and requires a compatible Decks receiver. For Open in Decks for Mac, check that the Mac app is installed. For iCloud, check Apple sign-in and connectivity, then review the transfer status in Ingest and Incoming Photos in Decks.

Decks waits for you to choose a new or existing project. Later leaves the transfer in Incoming Photos. Cloud-only Apple Photos images may first need to download. Review the saved transfer’s status before retrying.

Transfers contain independent photo copies, not Ingest workspaces or naming settings. The old built-in Social Export editor was removed in 0.9.6; old Social Export projects are not automatically converted. Send to Decks guide →

articles.title: Claude Second Opinion
articles.body: This optional feature needs Claude Code installed and signed in to your Claude subscription. It uses your account’s connection and usage limits. It is separate from the built-in on-device checks, which do not require Claude. Review what Ask sends to Anthropic before using it.

articles.title: Get in touch
articles.body: Email contact@brianrenshaw.app with your macOS version, the Ingest version from Settings, General, and your camera model. Tell me what you pressed and what happened. You never need to send me a photograph to report a problem.
