articles.title: Messages or Email sharing did not work
articles.body:
The wrong files are included

Use Send Photos for the selected visible photos. Send Folder ignores the grid selection and filter. Cards, volume roots, and sources with subfolders enabled include nested media. Check the count and size before continuing.

A draft does not open

Confirm that Messages or your email app is set up. Finish the current sharing draft before starting another from the same tab. For multiple files, retry with Create ZIP. If preparation fails, check that the source drive is connected and the files are readable.

The attachment is too large or will not preview

File sharing preserves the existing format, including RAW files. ZIP packages files together; it does not resize photos or guarantee a smaller attachment. Share fewer files or prepare smaller JPEGs for a recipient who needs them. Attachment limits depend on the receiving service.

Apple Photos videos cannot be shared

This sharing path supports still images from Apple Photos. Use Photos itself for videos. Read the sharing guide →

articles.title: Resume work after reconnecting a drive
articles.body:
Reconnect and reopen the same source

Connect the original drive, confirm it appears in Finder, and reopen its photo folder in Ingest. Ingest 0.9.9 preserves tags, ratings, and Organize drafts across disconnects and reconnects using the drive and file identity. A different drive with the same name is not treated as the original.

Resume an Organize draft

Open File → Organize… for the folder. A saved draft can resume even if the drive’s mount path changed. Check the operation, destination, and proposed paths before applying. Ingest validates file and destination identity; if it reports a changed source, reconnect the original rather than applying to a replacement.

An import was interrupted

Reconnecting does not mean a canceled import completed. Review its result and verified copies, then import what remains. Check an incomplete copy →

A recovery warning appears after using an older build

Keep the recovery files and contact support with the warning text and app versions. There is no in-app restore for conflicting edits preserved from an older build. Do not remove recovery data while investigating.

articles.title: How to read this
articles.body:
⌘ is Command, ⌥ is Option, ⌃ is Control, and ⇧ is Shift. A key written on its own, like T, is pressed on its own.

Some keys mean different things depending on where you are. In the file browser, there are three places: the grid of thumbnails, the large preview, and a video playing in the preview. Where a key only works in some of them, the table says so. Apple Photos has contextual commands too. Decks is a separate app.

Single letters pause whenever you are typing. If the cursor is in the keyword field, T types a letter t. Press Esc to leave the field and the keys come back.

A command that cannot run right now does not fail quietly. It beeps and the status bar says why, for example that nothing is tagged, or that the source is read only.

articles.title: Changing a key
articles.body:
Open Settings, then Shortcuts. Every command is listed with its key. Click the key and press the one you want. You can also Tab to the recorder and press Return or Space to begin. Esc cancels, and Delete removes the key so the command has none.

If the key is already taken by something that overlaps, Ingest names the other command and offers to move the key across. It refuses a key that is fixed, and it refuses the bare keys that move you around, because the app consumes those before any command sees them.

Standard Mac editing keys are reserved. Select All, Undo, Redo, and Settings retain their native shortcuts. If an older custom binding conflicts with a standard key, Settings explains the conflict and offers a reset; the saved override is kept until you change it.

While a text field has focus, ⌘A selects its text, and undo and redo stay in that editor. Photo-navigation keys do not intercept typing.

A changed key follows everywhere at once. The menus, the palette, the ? sheet, and the hold overlay all read from the same table, so there is no second place to update and nothing to get out of step. Reset All puts every key back.

articles.title: Every action, one search
articles.body:
Find Source Summary, Select from Pick List, Export Selected Decisions, and Open Current Source in New Tab by name. Source Summary opens in the inspector; clicking a count applies a removable filter.

If you can do it in Ingest, you can find it with ⌘K—whether the action has an assigned shortcut or not. Press ⌘K and search by name, alias, or category. Switch workspaces, find a folder, tag a keeper, edit metadata, organize files, or export without navigating menus.

Inside the palette, ⌘K toggles Actions. Use the arrow keys and Return to choose Pin/Unpin, Copy Link, or Configure Shortcut. Esc closes Actions before it closes the palette. Configure Shortcut reveals that command in Settings; temporary card and recent-folder entries do not offer it.

The palette also lists the things that come and go: your favorites, workspaces, splits, metadata presets, actions, and recent folders. ⇧⌘P pins whatever is highlighted to the top of the list. ⇧⌘C copies a link that runs it, which is how the URL scheme is meant to be discovered.

To show the shortcut overlay, tap and release ⌘, then press it again and hold. A single long hold does not open it. Settings offers an enable switch and 600, 900, or 1,200 ms second-hold delay. Quick Tips can teach current custom shortcuts as you work; disable teaching or reset its learning in Browsing Settings.
